The Management REST APIs of **Azure AI Search** (formerly known as *Azure Cognitive Search*) provide programmatic access to administrative operations:
1. Create, update, and delete a search service
2. Retrieve search service information
3. Create, regenerate, or retrieve `api-keys` (query or admin keys)
4. Add or remove replicas and partitions (adjust capacity)
5. Configure a search service to use a private endpoint
6. Enable or disable Azure role-based access control
For data plane tasks, such as creating and querying an index, use the [Search Service REST APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/searchservice/) instead.
## How to work with the management REST APIs
To fully administer your service programmatically, you work with two APIs: the Management REST API of Azure AI Search documented here, plus the common [Azure Resource Manager REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/resources/).
The Resource Manager API is used for general-purpose operations that aren't service specific, such as querying subscription data, listing geo-locations, and so forth. All Resource Manager API calls are authenticated using Microsoft Entra ID. You must have membership and a role assignment in a Microsoft Entra tenant to make Resource Manager API calls.
## Versioned API docs
REST API docs are versioned. When you open an API reference page, a version selector appears above the table of contents. The selector becomes available when you choose a page from the **Reference > Resource Manager** folder.
![Screenshot of the version selector.](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/searchmanagement/media/api-version.png)
## Permissions and access control
Administration rights are conveyed through built-in roles in Microsoft Entra ID:
1. **Owner** or **Contributor** assignments are required for most tasks.
2. **Reader** role has limited access to service information (GET operations, except for API keys, which require Owner or Contributor permissions).
For more information, see [Role-based access control in Azure AI Search](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-rbac).
A best practice is to assign roles to groups rather than individual users. An Azure subscription owner or global administrator manages these assignments.      --location eastus \
```azurecli
     --query "[?model.name=='gpt-5-mini'].{version:model.version,skus:join(',',model.skus[].name)}" \

```
2. Deploy the model:
```azurecli
 az cognitiveservices account deployment create \
     --name my-foundry-resource \
     --resource-group my-foundry-rg \
     --deployment-name gpt-5-mini \
     --model-name gpt-5-mini \
     --model-version "2025-08-07" \
     --model-format OpenAI \
     --sku-capacity 10 \
     --sku-name GlobalStandard
```
 If the command fails with `DeploymentModelNotSupported`, the model, version, or SKU isn't available in your region. Use the output of the previous step to choose a supported combination.
3. Verify the deployment succeeded:
```azurecli
 az cognitiveservices account deployment show \
     --name my-foundry-resource \
     --resource-group my-foundry-rg \
     --deployment-name gpt-5-mini \
     --query properties.provisioningState --output tsv
```
 The output shows `Succeeded` when the deployment is ready.

## Choose a tier
Foundry IQ offers two pricing models:
1. **Dedicated** offers multiple [pricing tiers](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/search/): Free, Basic, Standard, and Storage Optimized. Each tier has its own [capacity and limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/search-limits-quotas-capacity). On billable tiers, you pay an hourly rate for the replicas and partitions configured for your service.
2. **Serverless** is consumption-based: you pay for what you use, the service scales for you, and limits apply primarily at the index level.

If you plan to use [integrated vectorization](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/vector-search-integrated-vectorization) with the Azure Vision skill and vectorizer, Foundry IQ must be in the same region as the embedding models hosted on Azure Vision in Foundry Tools.
2. For the recommended [keyless authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/search-security-rbac), assign the **Search Service Contributor** and **Search Index Data Contributor** roles to your user account, managed identity, or service principal. For the less secure [key-based authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/search-security-api-keys), obtain an admin API key.
3. Source documents with [vector embeddings](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/vector-search-how-to-generate-embeddings) to upload to the index. You can also use [integrated vectorization](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/vector-search-integrated-vectorization) for this task.
4. The dimensions limit of your embedding model. `text-embedding-ada-002` is fixed at 1536, `text-embedding-3-small` ranges from 1 to 1536, and `text-embedding-3-large` ranges from 1 to 3072.

## Getting started
There are two types of keys used to access your search service: **admin***(read-write)* and **query***(read-only)* keys. Restricting access and operations in client apps is essential to safeguarding the search assets on your service. Always use a query key rather than an admin key for any query originating from a client app.
*Note: The example Azure CLI snippet above retrieves an admin key so it's easier to get started exploring APIs, but it should be managed carefully.*
#### Create a SearchClient
To instantiate the `SearchClient`, you'll need the **endpoint**, **API key** and **index name**:
```C
string indexName = "nycjobs";

// Get the service endpoint and API key from the environment
Uri endpoint = new Uri(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("SEARCH_ENDPOINT"));
string key = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("SEARCH_API_KEY");

// Create a client
AzureKeyCredential credential = new AzureKeyCredential(key);
SearchClient client = new SearchClient(endpoint, indexName, credential);
```
#### Create a client using Microsoft Entra ID authentication
You can also create a `SearchClient`, `SearchIndexClient`, or `SearchIndexerClient` using Microsoft Entra ID authentication. Your user or service principal must be assigned the "Search Index Data Reader" role. Using the [DefaultAzureCredential](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/Azure.Search.Documents_12.0.0/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md#defaultazurecredential) you can authenticate a service using Managed Identity or a service principal, authenticate as a developer working on an application, and more all without changing code. Check [Azure Vision in Foundry Tools regions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/computer-vision/overview-image-analysis#region-availability) for multimodal APIs that enable text and image vectorization. These APIs are powered by Azure Vision and accessed through a Microsoft Foundry resource. However, they're generally available in fewer regions than the Microsoft Foundry resource itself.
## Choose a tier
Foundry IQ offers two pricing models:
1. **Dedicated** offers multiple [pricing tiers](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/search/): Free, Basic, Standard, and Storage Optimized. Each tier has its own [capacity and limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/search-limits-quotas-capacity). On billable tiers, you pay an hourly rate for the replicas and partitions configured for your service.
2. **Serverless** is consumption-based: you pay for what you use, the service scales for you, and limits apply primarily at the index level.
The Basic and Standard tiers are the most common for high-utilization production workloads. Many customers choose Serverless and consumption-based billing as their lower-cost starting point. For information about the pricing models, computing characteristics, feature availability, and region availability, see [Choose a pricing model and service tier](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/search-sku-tier).
[![Screenshot of the Select Pricing Tier page in the Azure portal that shows the Dedicated tiers and the Serverless tier.](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/media/search-create-service-portal/select-pricing-tier.png)](media/search-create-service-portal/select-pricing-tier.png#lightbox)","contentUrl":"https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/search-create-service-portal#choose-a-region"},{"title":"Create a vector index in Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search)","content":"# Create a vector index in Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search)
## Prerequisites
1. A [Foundry IQ service](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/search-create-service-portal) in any region and on any tier. If you plan to use [integrated vectorization](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/vector-search-integrated-vectorization) with the Azure Vision skill and vectorizer, Foundry IQ must be in the same region as the embedding models hosted on Azure Vision in Foundry Tools.
2. For the recommended [keyless authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/search-security-rbac), assign the **Search Service Contributor** and **Search Index Data Contributor** roles to your user account, managed identity, or service principal. For the less secure [key-based authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/search-security-api-keys), obtain an admin API key.
3. Source documents with [vector embeddings](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/vector-search-how-to-generate-embeddings) to upload to the index. You can also use [integrated vectorization](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/vector-search-integrated-vectorization) for this task.
4. The dimensions limit of your embedding model. `text-embedding-ada-002` is fixed at 1536, `text-embedding-3-small` ranges from 1 to 1536, and `text-embedding-3-large` ranges from 1 to 3072.
5. The similarity metric for your embedding model. Azure OpenAI models use [`cosine`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/concepts/understand-embeddings#cosine-similarity).
6. Familiarity with [creating an index](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/search-how-to-create-search-index). A schema always includes a field for the document key, fields for search or filters, and other configurations for behaviors needed during indexing and queries.
Note
Some Foundry IQ services created before January 2019 can't create a vector index. If applicable, create a new service to use vectors.","contentUrl":"https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/vector-search-how-to-create-index#prerequisites"}]}

# Create a Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search) service in the Azure portal

Note

[Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search)](/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/what-is-foundry-iq) provides direct indexing and query APIs alongside higher-level knowledge source and knowledge base APIs for managed retrieval. Use the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), [REST APIs](/en-us/azure/search/search-api-versions#rest-apis), or [Azure SDKs](/en-us/azure/search/search-api-versions#all-azure-sdks) to configure these capabilities, or connect agents to knowledge bases in the [Microsoft Foundry portal](https://ai.azure.com/?cid=learnDocs).

[Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search)](search-what-is-azure-search) is an information retrieval platform for the enterprise. It supports traditional search and conversational, AI-driven search for "chat with your data" experiences across your proprietary content.

Most modern AI apps use Foundry IQ as part of a larger architecture (for example, with Microsoft Foundry agents, vectorization pipelines, or chat-based apps). This article focuses on creating the underlying Foundry IQ service.

The easiest way to create a Foundry IQ service is through the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), which is covered in this article.

[![Animated GIF showing how to create a Foundry IQ service in the Azure portal.](media/search-create-service-portal/animatedgif-azuresearch-small.gif)](media/search-create-service-portal/animatedgif-azuresearch.gif#lightbox)

You can also use:

- [Azure PowerShell](search-manage-powershell#create-or-delete-a-service)
- [Azure CLI](search-manage-azure-cli#create-or-delete-a-service)
- [Management REST API](search-manage-rest#create-or-update-a-service)
- [Azure Resource Manager template](search-get-started-arm)
- [Bicep](search-get-started-bicep)
- [Terraform](search-get-started-terraform)

## Before you start

Some properties are fixed for the lifetime of the Foundry IQ service. Before you create your service, decide on the following properties:

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Name | Becomes part of the URL endpoint. The name must be unique and follow naming rules. |
| [Region](search-region-support) | Determines data residency and availability of certain features. For example, semantic ranker and Azure AI integration have region requirements. Choose a region that supports the features you need. |
| [Tier](search-sku-tier) | Determines infrastructure, service limits, and billing. Some features aren't available on lower or specialized tiers. After you create your service, you need to [Choose a pricing model and service tier](search-sku-tier). |
| [Compute type](search-security-best-practices#optional-enable-confidential-computing) | Determines virtualization and security model. You can choose between standard VMs (recommended) and confidential VMs, which are intended for select workloads requiring data-in-use privacy and isolation. |

## Subscribe to Azure

Foundry IQ requires a free or Standard Azure subscription.

To try Foundry IQ for free, [start a trial subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/purchase-options/azure-account?cid=msft_learn) and then create your Foundry IQ service on the Free tier. Each Azure subscription can have one free Foundry IQ service, which is intended for short-term, non-production evaluation of the product. You can complete all of the quickstarts and most of the tutorials on the Free tier. For more information, see [Try Foundry IQ for free](search-try-for-free).

Important

To make room for other services, Microsoft might delete free services that are inactive for an extended period of time.

## Find the Foundry IQ offering

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com).
2. In the upper-left corner of your dashboard, select **Create a resource**.

    [![Screenshot of the Create a Resource button in the Azure portal.](media/search-create-service-portal/create-resource.png)](media/search-create-service-portal/create-resource.png#lightbox)
3. Use the search box to find **Foundry IQ**.

    [![Screenshot of the Foundry IQ tile in the Azure portal.](media/search-create-service-portal/azure-ai-search-tile.png)](media/search-create-service-portal/azure-ai-search-tile.png#lightbox)

## Choose a subscription

If you have multiple Azure subscriptions, choose one for your Foundry IQ service.

## Scale your service

After deploying your Foundry IQ service, you can [scale it to meet your needs](search-limits-quotas-capacity). Foundry IQ offers two scaling dimensions: *replicas* and *partitions*. Replicas increase your service's capacity to handle more search query traffic. Partitions increase your service's capacity to store and search through more documents.

You can scale replicas and partitions only on Dedicated tiers. On the Free tier, you can't scale your service or configure replicas and partitions. On Serverless, the service scales for you.

Important

A Dedicated service must have [two replicas for read-only SLA and three replicas for read/write SLA](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/sla/search/v1_0/). Every Serverless service has a read/write SLA for its lifetime.

Adding resources increases your monthly bill. Use the [pricing calculator](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/calculator/) to understand the billing implications. You can adjust resources based on load, such as increasing resources for initial indexing and decreasing them later for incremental indexing.

To scale your service:

1. Go to your Foundry IQ service in the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com).
2. From the left pane, select **Settings** > **Scale**.

    [![Screenshot of the Scale tab with sliders for adding replicas and partitions.](media/search-create-service-portal/scale-settings.png)](media/search-create-service-portal/scale-settings.png#lightbox)
3. Use the sliders to add replicas and partitions.

## When to add a second service

Most customers use a single Foundry IQ service at a tier [sufficient for the expected load](search-capacity-planning). One service can host multiple indexes, each isolated from the others, within the [maximum limits of your chosen tier](search-limits-quotas-capacity#index-limits). In Foundry IQ, you can direct requests to only one index, reducing the chance of retrieving data from other indexes in the same service.

However, you might need a second service for the following operational requirements:

- Region outages. In the unlikely event of a full region outage, Foundry IQ doesn't provide instant failover. You must implement your own multi-region solution and failover approach. For more information, see [Multi-region deployments in Foundry IQ](search-multi-region).
- [Multitenant architectures](search-modeling-multitenant-saas-applications) that require two or more services.
- Globally deployed applications that require services in each geography to minimize latency.

Note

In Foundry IQ, you can't separate indexing and querying operations, so don't create multiple services for separate workloads. An index is always queried on the service in which it was created, and you can't copy an index to another service.

A second service isn't required for high availability. For a Dedicated service, you achieve high availability for queries by using two or more replicas in the same service. Because the replicas are updated sequentially, at least one is operational when a service update is rolled out. In contrast, every Serverless service has built-in high availability and a read/write SLA for its lifetime. For more information about uptime, see [Service Level Agreements](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/sla/search/v1_0/).

## Add more services to your subscription

Foundry IQ limits the [number of Foundry IQ services](search-limits-quotas-capacity#subscription-limits) you can initially create in a subscription. If you reach your limit, you can request more quotas. The **Quotas** service doesn't support quota management on the Serverless tier. To change the number of Serverless services you can create, open a support request.

You must have Owner or Contributor permissions for the subscription to request quota. Depending on your region and data center capacity, you might be able to automatically request quota to add services to your subscription. If the request fails, reduce the number or file a support ticket. Expect a one-month turnaround for a large quota increase, such as more than 30 extra services.

To request more subscription quota:

1. Go to your dashboard in the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com).
2. Use the search box to find the **Quotas** service.

    [![Screenshot of the Quota search term and the Quotas service in the results.](media/search-create-service-portal/quota-search.png)](media/search-create-service-portal/quota-search.png#lightbox)
3. On the **Overview** tab, select the **Search** tile.

    [![Screenshot of the Search tile on the Overview page.](media/search-create-service-portal/quota-overview-page.png)](media/search-create-service-portal/quota-overview-page.png#lightbox)
4. Set filters to review the existing quota for Foundry IQ services in your current subscription. Filter by usage.

    [![Screenshot of the Usage filter for search services in your current subscription.](media/search-create-service-portal/usage-filter.png)](media/search-create-service-portal/usage-filter.png#lightbox)
5. Next to the tier and region that need more quotas, select **Request adjustment**![Screenshot of the Request Adjustment icon, which is the outline of a pencil.](media/search-create-service-portal/request-adjustment-icon.png).
6. In **New Quota Request**, enter a new limit for your subscription quota. The new limit must be greater than your current limit. If regional capacity is constrained, your request isn't automatically approved, and an incident report is generated on your behalf for investigation and resolution.
7. Submit your request.
8. Monitor notifications in the Azure portal for updates on the new limit. Most requests are approved within 24 hours.

Note

[Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search)](/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/what-is-foundry-iq) provides direct indexing and query APIs alongside higher-level knowledge source and knowledge base APIs for managed retrieval. Use the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), [REST APIs](/en-us/azure/search/search-api-versions#rest-apis), or [Azure SDKs](/en-us/azure/search/search-api-versions#all-azure-sdks) to configure these capabilities, or connect agents to knowledge bases in the [Microsoft Foundry portal](https://ai.azure.com/?cid=learnDocs).

Vector search is an information retrieval approach that supports indexing and querying over numeric representations of content. Because the content is numeric rather than plain text, matching is based on vectors that are most similar to the query vector. This approach enables matching across:

- Semantic or conceptual likeness. For example, "dog" and "canine" are conceptually similar but linguistically distinct.
- Multilingual content, such as "dog" in English and "hund" in German.
- Multiple content types, such as "dog" in plain text and an image of a dog.

This article provides an overview of vector search in Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search), including supported scenarios, availability, and integration with other Azure services.

Tip

Want to get started right away? Follow these steps:

1. [Provide embeddings](vector-search-how-to-generate-embeddings) for your index or [generate embeddings](vector-search-integrated-vectorization) in an indexer pipeline.
2. [Create a vector index](vector-search-how-to-create-index).
3. [Run vector queries](vector-search-how-to-query).

## What scenarios can vector search support?

Vector search supports the following scenarios:

- **Similarity search**. Encode text using embedding models or open-source models, such as OpenAI embeddings or SBERT, respectively. You then retrieve documents using queries that are also encoded as vectors.
- **[Hybrid search](hybrid-search-overview)**. Foundry IQ defines hybrid search as the execution of vector search and [keyword search](search-lucene-query-architecture) in the same request. Vector support is implemented at the field level. If an index contains vector and nonvector fields, you can write a query that targets both. The queries execute in parallel, and the results are merged into a single response and ranked accordingly.
- **[Multimodal search](multimodal-search-overview)**. Encode text and images using multimodal embeddings, such as [OpenAI CLIP](https://github.com/openai/CLIP) or [GPT-4 Turbo with Vision](/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/whats-new#gpt-4-turbo-with-vision-now-available) in Azure OpenAI, and then query an embedding space composed of vectors from both content types.
- **Multilingual search**. Foundry IQ is designed for extensibility. If you have embedding models and chat models trained in multiple languages, you can call them through custom or built-in skills on the indexing side or vectorizers on the query side. For more control over text translation, use the [multi-language capabilities](search-language-support) supported by Foundry IQ for nonvector content in hybrid search scenarios.
- **Filtered vector search**. A query request can include a vector query and a [filter expression](search-filters). Filters apply to text and numeric fields. They're useful for metadata filters and for including or excluding search results based on filter criteria. Although a vector field isn't filterable, you can set up a filterable text or numeric field. The search engine can process the filter before or after executing the vector query.
- **Vector database**. Foundry IQ stores the data that you query over. Use it as a [pure vector index](vector-store) when you need long-term memory or a knowledge base, grounding data for the [retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)](retrieval-augmented-generation-overview) architecture, or an app that uses vectors.

## How does vector search work?

Foundry IQ supports indexing, storing, and querying vector embeddings from a search index. The following diagram shows the indexing and query workflows for vector search.

[![Architecture of vector search workflow.](media/vector-search-overview/vector-search-architecture-diagram-3.svg)](media/vector-search-overview/vector-search-architecture-diagram-3-high-res.png#lightbox)

On the indexing side, Foundry IQ uses a [nearest neighbors algorithm](vector-search-ranking) to place similar vectors close together in an index. Internally, it creates [vector indexes](vector-store) for each vector field.

How you get embeddings from your source content into Foundry IQ depends on your processing approach:

- For internal processing, Foundry IQ offers [integrated data chunking and vectorization](vector-search-integrated-vectorization) in an indexer pipeline. You provide the necessary resources, such as endpoints and connection information for Azure OpenAI. Foundry IQ then makes the calls and handles the transitions. This approach requires an indexer, a supported data source, and a skillset that drives chunking and embedding.
- For external processing, you can [generate embeddings](vector-search-how-to-generate-embeddings) outside of Foundry IQ and push the prevectorized content directly into [vector fields](vector-search-how-to-create-index) in your search index.

On the query side, your client app collects user input, typically through a prompt. You can add an encoding step to vectorize the input and then send the vector query to your Foundry IQ index for similarity search. As with indexing, you can use [integrated vectorization](vector-search-integrated-vectorization) to encode the query. For either approach, Foundry IQ returns documents with the requested `k` nearest neighbors (kNN) in the results.

Foundry IQ supports [hybrid scenarios](hybrid-search-overview) that run vector and keyword search in parallel and return a unified result set, which often provides better results than vector or keyword search alone. For hybrid search, both vector and nonvector content are ingested into the same index for queries that run simultaneously.

## Availability and pricing

Vector search is available in [all regions](search-region-support) and on [all tiers](search-sku-tier) at no extra charge. However, generating embeddings or using AI enrichment for vectorization might incur charges from the model provider.

For portal and programmatic access to vector search, you can use:

- The [**Import data** wizard](search-get-started-portal-import-vectors) in the Azure portal.
- The [Search Service REST APIs](/en-us/rest/api/searchservice).
- The Azure SDKs for [.NET](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Azure.Search.Documents), [Python](https://pypi.org/project/azure-search-documents), and [JavaScript](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@azure/search-documents).
- Other Azure offerings, such as Microsoft Foundry.

Note

- Some Foundry IQ services created before January 1, 2019 don't support vector workloads. If you try to add a vector field to a schema and get an error, it's a result of outdated services. In this situation, you must create a new Foundry IQ service to try out the vector feature.
- Foundry IQ services created after April 3, 2024 offer [higher quotas for vector indexes](vector-search-index-size). If you have an older service, you might be able to [upgrade your service](search-how-to-upgrade) for higher vector quotas.

## Azure integration and related services

Foundry IQ is deeply integrated across the Azure AI platform. The following table lists products that are useful in vector workloads.

| Product | Integration |
| --- | --- |
| Azure OpenAI | Azure OpenAI provides embedding models and chat models. Demos and samples target the [text-embedding-ada-002](/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/concepts/models#embeddings-models) model. We recommend Azure OpenAI for generating embeddings for text. |
| Foundry Tools | [Image Retrieval Vectorize Image API](/en-us/azure/ai-services/computer-vision/how-to/image-retrieval#call-the-vectorize-image-api) supports vectorization of image content. We recommend this API for generating embeddings for images. |
| Foundry Agent Service | In Foundry IQ, you can create an *indexed [knowledge source](agentic-knowledge-source-overview)* that points to a search index containing vector fields and a vectorizer. You can then parent the knowledge source to a *[knowledge base](agentic-retrieval-how-to-create-knowledge-base)* and [connect the knowledge base to Foundry Agent Service](/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/agents/how-to/foundry-iq-connect), providing your agents with vector search results for enhanced knowledge retrieval. |
| Azure data platforms: Azure Blob Storage, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure SQL, Microsoft OneLake | You can use [indexers](search-indexer-overview) to automate data ingestion, and then use [integrated vectorization](vector-search-integrated-vectorization) to generate embeddings. Foundry IQ can automatically index vector data from [Azure blob indexers](search-how-to-index-azure-blob-storage), [Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL indexers](search-how-to-index-cosmosdb-sql), [Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2](search-how-to-index-azure-data-lake-storage), [Azure Table Storage](search-how-to-index-azure-tables), and [Microsoft OneLake](search-how-to-index-onelake-files). For more information, see [Add vector fields to a search index](vector-search-how-to-create-index). |

Foundry IQ is also commonly used in open-source frameworks like [LangChain](https://js.langchain.com/docs/integrations/vectorstores/azure_aisearch).

## Connect Application Insights for agent tracing

Before you run an agent quickstart, complete this setup in the Foundry portal.

Review [tracing security and privacy](../observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup#security-and-privacy) and [data retention and cost](../observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup#data-retention-and-cost) before enabling tracing.

Follow [Connect Application Insights to your Foundry project](../observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup#connect-application-insights-to-your-foundry-project). Verify and reuse an existing connection.

Note

If your existing connection uses **Project Managed Identity**, or your organization requires Entra-only ingestion, keep your approved configuration. See [Configure Microsoft Entra authentication for trace ingestion](../observability/how-to/trace-ingestion-entra-authentication).

For Foundry-hosted agents, the connection enables [server-side tracing](../observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup#server-side-traces-in-the-foundry-portal). For agents running in your own application, also [configure client-side tracing](../observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup#client-side-traces-with-the-microsoft-foundry-sdk).

### Grant access to traces

The person or group viewing traces needs **Log Analytics Reader** on the connected Application Insights resource, or equivalent inherited access. For protected trace tables, also grant **Privileged Monitoring Data Reader**.

See [Tracing prerequisites](../observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup#prerequisites) and [Assign Azure roles using the Azure portal](/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments-portal) for detailed instructions.

For workspace-scoped queries or workspaces that require workspace permissions, see [Manage access to Log Analytics workspaces](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/manage-access).

### Verify your first agent trace

Continue with model deployment or your agent quickstart. After your first agent request, follow [Verify tracing works](../observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup#verify-tracing-works) to confirm that a new trace appears. A successful response alone doesn't confirm that traces were stored.

If no trace appears, see [Tracing troubleshooting](../observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup#troubleshooting).

## Deploy a model

Deploy a model that you can use. This example uses **gpt-5-mini**, but you can choose any available model.

Tip

# [Azure CLI](#tab/azurecli)
1. List the models available in your region so you can confirm the model name and version:

    ```azurecli
    az cognitiveservices model list \
        --location eastus \
        --query "[?model.name=='gpt-5-mini'].{version:model.version,skus:join(',',model.skus[].name)}" \
        --output table
    ```

2. Deploy the model:

    ```azurecli
    az cognitiveservices account deployment create \
        --name my-foundry-resource \
        --resource-group my-foundry-rg \
        --deployment-name gpt-5-mini \
        --model-name gpt-5-mini \
        --model-version "2025-08-07" \
        --model-format OpenAI \
        --sku-capacity 10 \
        --sku-name GlobalStandard
    ```

    If the command fails with `DeploymentModelNotSupported`, the model, version, or SKU isn't available in your region. Use the output of the previous step to choose a supported combination.
3. Verify the deployment succeeded:

    ```azurecli
    az cognitiveservices account deployment show \
        --name my-foundry-resource \
        --resource-group my-foundry-rg \
        --deployment-name gpt-5-mini \
        --query properties.provisioningState --output tsv
    ```

    The output shows `Succeeded` when the deployment is ready.

Reference: [az cognitiveservices account deployment](/en-us/cli/azure/cognitiveservices/account/deployment)

# [Foundry portal](#tab/portal)
1. Navigate to **Build** > **Catalog** > **Model Catalog**.
2. Search for **gpt-5-mini**.
3. Select **Deploy** > **Default settings** to add it to your project.
4. Note the deployment name (for example, `gpt-5-mini`). Your team needs this name to use the model.

---

## Get your project connection details

You need your project endpoint to connect from code. If you're administering this project for others, send them this endpoint along with the deployment name.

# [Azure CLI](#tab/azurecli)
Get the project endpoint:

```azurecli
az cognitiveservices account project show \
    --name my-foundry-resource \
    --resource-group my-foundry-rg \
    --project-name my-foundry-project \
    --query 'properties.endpoints."AI Foundry API"' --output tsv
```

The output is your project endpoint, in the form `https://my-foundry-resource.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/my-foundry-project`. Use this value in other quickstarts and tutorials.

# [Foundry portal](#tab/portal)
1. Sign in to [Microsoft Foundry](https://ai.azure.com/?cid=learnDocs) by using your Azure account.
2. Select your project.
3. Find your project endpoint on the welcome screen of the project.![Screenshot of Microsoft Foundry Models welcome screen showing the endpoint URL and copy button.](../media/quickstarts/project-endpoint.png)
4. Copy the endpoint value. You use this value in other quickstarts and tutorials.

---

## For administrators - grant access

If you're administering a team, assign the **Foundry User** role to team members so they can use the project and deployed models. This role provides the minimum permissions needed to build and test AI applications. For other roles you might need to assign, see [Role-based access control for Microsoft Foundry](../concepts/rbac-foundry).

# [Azure CLI](#tab/azurecli)
1. Get the project's resource ID:

    ```azurecli
    PROJECT_ID=$(az cognitiveservices account project show \
        --name my-foundry-resource \
        --resource-group my-foundry-rg \
        --project-name my-foundry-project \
        --query id -o tsv)
    ```
2. Assign the **Foundry User** role to a team member:

    Important

    The Foundry RBAC roles were recently renamed. **Foundry User**, **Foundry Owner**, **Foundry Account Owner**, and **Foundry Project Manager** were previously named Azure AI User, Azure AI Owner, Azure AI Account Owner, and Azure AI Project Manager. You might still see the previous names in some places while the rename rolls out. The role IDs and core permissions are unchanged by the rename.

    ```azurecli
    az role assignment create \
        --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" \
        --assignee "user-d24dfead@example.com" \
        --assignee-principal-type User \
        --scope $PROJECT_ID
    ```

Note

Because the Foundry RBAC roles were recently renamed, use the role definition ID (GUID) instead of the role name in your code to avoid issues during the rename rollout:

- **Foundry User**: `53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d`
- **Foundry Owner**: `c883944f-8b7b-4483-af10-35834be79c4a`
- **Foundry Account Owner**: `e47c6f54-e4a2-4754-9501-8e0985b135e1`
- **Foundry Project Manager**: `eadc314b-1a2d-4efa-be10-5d325db5065e`

To add a security group instead of an individual user:

```azurecli
az role assignment create \
    --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" \
    --assignee-object-id "<security-group-object-id>" \
    --assignee-principal-type Group \
    --scope $PROJECT_ID
```

1. Verify the role assignment:

    ```azurecli
    az role assignment list \
        --scope $PROJECT_ID \
        --role "53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d" \
        --output table
    ```

Reference: [az role assignment](/en-us/cli/azure/role/assignment)

# [Foundry portal](#tab/portal)
1. In the Foundry portal, select **Manage** in the upper-right navigation.
2. Select **Project details** in the left pane.
3. Select the **Users** tab.
4. Select **Add user** in the upper right.
5. Enter the email address of the team member.
6. Select **Add**.

Repeat these steps for each team member or security group.

Tip

To add multiple users at once, use a Microsoft Entra security group instead of individual email addresses.

---

## Verify team member access

Ask a team member to verify their access by signing in to [Microsoft Foundry](https://ai.azure.com) and selecting the project from the project list.

If the team member can't access the project, verify that the role assignment completed successfully. Check that you used the correct email address or security group ID. Make sure the team member's Azure account is in the same Microsoft Entra tenant.

To confirm the deployed model is available, ask the team member to select **Build** in the upper-right navigation, then **Models** in the left pane.

## Clean up resources

When you no longer want this project, delete the resource group to delete all resources associated with it.

# [Azure CLI](#tab/azurecli)
```azurecli
az group delete --name my-foundry-rg --yes --no-wait
```

Deletion runs in the background. To confirm that the resource group is gone, run:

```azurecli
az group exists --name my-foundry-rg
```

The output shows `false` when deletion finishes.

# [Foundry portal](#tab/portal)
In the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), find and select your resource group. Select **Delete** and confirm to delete the resource group and all its associated resources.

 """Embed canonical chunks from MongoDB and index them into an Azure AI Search index.
 
 Creates or updates the versioned index, then reprocesses every stored canonical document.
 Unchanged documents are re-uploaded idempotently (stable chunk IDs). Run after
 `run_source_ingestion.py`; rerun whenever new documents are stored.
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import argparse
 import asyncio
 import sys
 
 from azure.core.credentials import AzureKeyCredential
 from azure.search.documents.aio import SearchClient
 from azure.search.documents.indexes.aio import SearchIndexClient
 
 from product_support_agent.config import ModelAndSearchSettings, Settings
 from product_support_agent.document_store import MongoCanonicalDocumentRepository
 from product_support_agent.documents import HTML_PARSER_VERSION
 from product_support_agent.embeddings import OpenAICompatibleEmbedder
 from product_support_agent.indexing import DocumentIndexingService
 from product_support_agent.search import (
     AzureAISearchProvider,
     apply_search_index,
     build_search_index,
     build_versioned_index_name,
 )
 
 
 def index_name_for(base: str, settings: ModelAndSearchSettings) -> str:
     return build_versioned_index_name(
         base,
         embedding_model_version=settings.embedding_model_version,
         embedding_dimensions=settings.embedding_dimensions,
         parser_version=HTML_PARSER_VERSION,
     )
 
 
 def build_embedder(settings: ModelAndSearchSettings) -> OpenAICompatibleEmbedder:
     return OpenAICompatibleEmbedder(
         base_url=settings.embedding_base_url,
         api_key=settings.embedding_api_key.get_secret_value(),
         deployment=settings.embedding_deployment,
         model_version=settings.embedding_model_version,
         dimensions=settings.embedding_dimensions,
     )
 
 
 async def _run(index_base: str) -> int:
     app_settings = Settings()
     settings = ModelAndSearchSettings()  # type: ignore[call-arg]
     mongo_uri = (
         app_settings.mongodb_uri.get_secret_value().strip() if app_settings.mongodb_uri else ""
     )
     if not mongo_uri:
         print("PRODUCT_SUPPORT_MONGODB_URI must be set", file=sys.stderr)
         return 2
 
     index_name = index_name_for(index_base, settings)
     credential = AzureKeyCredential(settings.search_key.get_secret_value())
     index_client = SearchIndexClient(settings.search_endpoint, credential)
     try:
         await apply_search_index(
             index_client,
             build_search_index(index_name, embedding_dimensions=settings.embedding_dimensions),
         )
     finally:
         await index_client.close()
 
     repository = MongoCanonicalDocumentRepository(mongo_uri)
     provider = AzureAISearchProvider(
         SearchClient(settings.search_endpoint, index_name, credential),
         embedding_dimensions=settings.embedding_dimensions,
         embedding_model_version=settings.embedding_model_version,
     )
     try:
         service = DocumentIndexingService(
             repository=repository,
             search=provider,
             embedder=build_embedder(settings),
         )
         count = await service.reconcile_all()
     finally:
         await provider.close()
         repository.close()
     print(f"Indexed {count} canonical documents into {index_name}")
     return 0
 
 
 def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
     parser.add_argument(
         "--index-base",
         default=None,
         help="index base name (defaults to PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_DEMO_INDEX_BASE)",
     )
     args = parser.parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
     base = args.index_base or ModelAndSearchSettings().demo_index_base  # type: ignore[call-arg]
     return asyncio.run(_run(base))
 
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     raise SystemExit(main())

 """Run one bounded, resumable documentation ingestion pass from the approved source map.
 
 Intended to be scheduled (for example weekly). Durable fetch state in MongoDB lets a rerun or a
 restart after a crash skip URLs fetched successfully within the freshness window.
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import argparse
 import asyncio
 import json
 import socket
 import sys
 from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
 from pathlib import Path
 from uuid import uuid4
 
 from product_support_agent.config import Settings
 from product_support_agent.document_store import MongoCanonicalDocumentRepository
 from product_support_agent.fetch_state import FreshnessPolicy, MongoFetchStateStore
 from product_support_agent.http_fetch import BoundedFetcher
 from product_support_agent.indexing import RepositoryOnlyIndexer
 from product_support_agent.source_ingestion import SourceIngestionLimits, SourceIngestionWorker
 from product_support_agent.sources import load_source_map
 
 LEASE_NAME = "source-ingestion"
 
 
 def _parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
     parser.add_argument("--product", action="append", default=None, help="limit to a product ID")
     parser.add_argument(
         "--discover-only",
         action="store_true",
         help="fetch robots.txt and seeds and report the selection without fetching pages",
     )
     parser.add_argument(
         "--force",
         action="store_true",
         help="ignore freshness and failure backoff for this run",
     )
     parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path, default=None, help="write the JSON run report")
     return parser.parse_args(argv)
 
 
 async def _run(args: argparse.Namespace, settings: Settings) -> int:
     mongo_uri = settings.mongodb_uri.get_secret_value().strip() if settings.mongodb_uri else ""
     if not mongo_uri:
         print("PRODUCT_SUPPORT_MONGODB_URI must be set", file=sys.stderr)
         return 2
     source_map = load_source_map(Path(settings.source_map_path))
     state = MongoFetchStateStore(mongo_uri)
     repository = MongoCanonicalDocumentRepository(mongo_uri)
     holder = f"{socket.gethostname()}:{uuid4()}"
     now = datetime.now(UTC)
     lease_ttl = timedelta(hours=6)
     try:
         state.ensure_indexes()
         repository.ensure_indexes()
         if not state.acquire_lease(LEASE_NAME, holder, now=now, ttl=lease_ttl):
             print("another source ingestion run holds the lease; exiting", file=sys.stderr)
             return 3
         worker = SourceIngestionWorker(
             source_map=source_map,
             state=state,
             fetcher=BoundedFetcher(
                 user_agent=settings.source_user_agent,
                 max_retry_after_seconds=settings.source_max_retry_after_seconds,
             ),
             indexer=RepositoryOnlyIndexer(repository=repository),
             repository=repository,
             policy=FreshnessPolicy(
                 success_freshness=timedelta(hours=settings.source_success_freshness_hours),
                 transient_failure_backoff=timedelta(
                     hours=settings.source_transient_failure_backoff_hours
                 ),
                 permanent_failure_backoff=timedelta(
                     days=settings.source_permanent_failure_backoff_days
                 ),
             ),
             limits=SourceIngestionLimits(
                 request_budget=settings.source_request_budget,
                 min_request_interval_seconds=settings.source_min_request_interval_seconds,
                 fail_fast_consecutive_failures=settings.source_fail_fast_consecutive_failures,
             ),
         )
         report = await worker.run(
             args.product,
             force=args.force,
             discover_only=args.discover_only,
         )
     finally:
         state.release_lease(LEASE_NAME, holder)
         state.close()
         repository.close()
 
     payload = report.model_dump(mode="json")
     if args.report is not None:
         args.report.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
     for product in report.products:
         print(
             f"{product.product_id:>6} {product.outcome:<16} {product.reason_category:<28} "
             f"selected={product.pages_selected} indexed={product.pages_indexed} "
             f"unchanged={product.pages_unchanged} fresh={product.pages_skipped_fresh} "
             f"failed={product.pages_failed} removed={product.pages_removed} "
             f"requests={product.requests}"
         )
     print(f"requests={report.requests}/{report.request_budget} stopped={report.stopped_reason}")
     return 0
 
 
 def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
     args = _parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
     return asyncio.run(_run(args, Settings()))
 
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     raise SystemExit(main())

 )
 
 
 def _required_environment_variable(name: str) -> str:
     value = os.environ.get(name, "").strip()
     if not value:
         raise ValueError(f"{name} must be set")
     return value
 
 
 async def _apply(
     *,
     endpoint: str,
     admin_key: str,
     index_name: str,
     embedding_dimensions: int,
 ) -> str:
     client = SearchIndexClient(endpoint, AzureKeyCredential(admin_key))
     try:
         result = await apply_search_index(
             client,
             build_search_index(
                 index_name,
                 embedding_dimensions=embedding_dimensions,
             ),
         )
         return result.name
     finally:
         await client.close()
 
 
 def main() -> int:
     try:
         endpoint = _required_environment_variable("PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_ENDPOINT")
         admin_key = _required_environment_variable("PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_ADMIN_KEY")
         embedding_model_version = _required_environment_variable(
             "PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_EMBEDDING_MODEL_VERSION"
         )
         index_base = _required_environment_variable("PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_TEST_INDEX_BASE")
         dimensions_text = _required_environment_variable(
             "PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS"
         )
         if not re.search(r"(?:^|-)test(?:-|$)", index_base.lower()):
             raise ValueError("the index base name must identify a dedicated test index")
         try:
             dimensions = int(dimensions_text)
         except ValueError as error:
             raise ValueError("embedding dimensions must be a positive integer") from error
 
         index_name = build_versioned_index_name(
             index_base,
             embedding_model_version=embedding_model_version,
             embedding_dimensions=dimensions,
             schema_version=INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION,
             parser_version=HTML_PARSER_VERSION,
         )
         applied_name = asyncio.run(
             _apply(
                 endpoint=endpoint,
                 admin_key=admin_key,
                 index_name=index_name,
                 embedding_dimensions=dimensions,
             )
         )
     except ValueError as error:
         print(str(error), file=sys.stderr)
         return 2
 
     print(f"Applied Azure AI Search test index: {applied_name}")
     return 0
 
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     raise SystemExit(main())

 title: Product Support Agent
 description: Local demo of a grounded product support assistant, including architecture, setup, configuration, Azure prerequisites, and quality checks
 author: Product Support Agent Team
 ms.date: 2026-11-22
 ms.topic: overview
 keywords:
   - product support
   - local demo
   - Microsoft Foundry
   - Azure AI Search
 ---
 
 ## Executive summary
 
 Product Support Agent is a local-first demonstration of a web and agentic
 support assistant. It answers questions from anonymously accessible product
 documentation, retrieves evidence from Azure AI Search, and returns links
 resolved by the server from that evidence.
 
 The browser calls only the TypeScript/Next.js server. Next.js calls the Python
 FastAPI service, which uses Microsoft Foundry for chat and embeddings and Azure
 AI Search for hybrid retrieval. MongoDB stores canonical documents and
 ingestion state; Azurite emulates Azure Queue Storage for local development.
 These two supporting services run in Podman, not in Azure.
 
 The approved source map covers 10 of the 100 manifest products. It has ingested
 300 pages and indexed 952 chunks. The Phase 6 evaluation reached 80.0% expected
 source hits in the top five, 100% citation URL matches, and 3/3 refusals for
 unanswerable questions. See the [evaluation report](docs/operations/phase-6-evaluation-v1.md).
 
 This is a local demo, not a production service. The cloud application stack is
 not deployed. Production-only controls and blocking triggers are listed in the
 [production gap register](docs/operations/production-gap-register.md), and the
 delivery boundaries are recorded in [ADR-0007](docs/architecture/decisions/adr-0007-demo-delivery-mode.md).
 
 ## Quick links by audience
 
 | Audience | Start here |
 |---|---|
 | Executive and product stakeholders | This overview, [demo outcomes](docs/operations/phase-6-evaluation-v1.md), [implementation status](docs/implementation-plan.md), and [production gap register](docs/operations/production-gap-register.md) |
 | Technical architects | [Architecture overview](docs/architecture/architecture-overview.md), [decision register](docs/architecture/decision-register.md), [ADRs](docs/architecture/decisions/), [risk assumptions](docs/architecture/risk-assumptions.md), and [security posture](docs/security/security-posture.md) |
 | Developers | [Local development runbook](docs/operations/local-development.md), [environment configuration](#configuration-and-environment-variables), [backend](src/product_support_agent/), and [web app](apps/web/) |
 | Quality assurance | [Test and evaluation guidance](#quality-assurance), [evaluation report](docs/operations/phase-6-evaluation-v1.md), [test suite](tests/), and [threat register](docs/security/threat-register.md) |
 
 ## What the demo includes
 
 * A Next.js interface with coverage disclosure, chat, transient client-side
   exchange state, and citation links.
 * A FastAPI endpoint that coordinates Microsoft Agent Framework, hybrid search,
   request limits, metadata-only logs, and server-side citation binding.
 * A resumable, request-bounded ingestion worker that reads only the versioned
   source map and respects source access controls.
 * A synthetic evaluation set covering 15 answerable questions and 3
   unanswerable questions.
 * A Podman Compose stack that binds published ports to `127.0.0.1`.
 
 The model is not allowed to supply citation URLs. Retrieved source text and
 user input are untrusted. Query and response retention is disabled. See the
 [threat register](docs/security/threat-register.md) and
 [privacy impact assessment](docs/security/privacy-impact-assessment.md).
 
 ## Local demo prerequisites
 
 * Windows PowerShell, Git, and Podman with a running Podman machine and a
   working `podman compose` provider.
 * Network access from the developer machine to the configured Microsoft
   Foundry and Azure AI Search endpoints.
 * An existing Microsoft Foundry deployment for chat and an embedding
   deployment, plus an Azure AI Search service.
 * `uv` 0.13.9 or later for the evaluation and Python checks. Node.js is not
   required to run the containerized demo; it is required to work on the web app
   directly.
 * For local development outside the containers, Python 3.11 or later and
   Node.js 22 or later.
 
 The [local development runbook](docs/operations/local-development.md) contains
 the clean-checkout setup, first-run ingestion and indexing, evaluation, and
 data-preserving stop commands.
 
 ### Azure resources for a local-only demo
 
 The application still calls two Azure services from the developer machine.
 Only the Foundry models and Azure AI Search need to be provisioned in Azure for
 the local demo. MongoDB and Azurite run locally in Compose.
 
 | Azure service | Set up or verify | Values needed by this repository |
 |---|---|---|
 | Microsoft Foundry | Use an existing Foundry resource/project with a chat deployment (`gpt-5`) and an embedding deployment (`text-embedding-3-small`). Verify region availability, quota, and that both deployments are ready. Creating a resource or model deployment can incur cost and needs the appropriate authorization. | The OpenAI-compatible `.../openai/v1` endpoint, API key, and the exact chat and embedding deployment names |
 | Azure AI Search | Use an existing Search service with vector-search support. The indexer script creates versioned `product-support-demo-*` indexes; a separate `product-support-test-*` index is used for opt-in live tests. Capture the service endpoint and an admin key for server-side indexing and query operations. Never put this key in browser code. | Search endpoint and admin API key; embedding model version and dimensions must match the Foundry embedding deployment (`1536` for the supplied example) |
 
 The current Azure documentation lists vector search across service tiers, but
 service quotas, capacity, pricing, and other features vary. Check current
 regional availability and costs before creating or changing a service. Semantic
 ranking was not evaluated for this demo because the Search tier and billing
 plan could not be verified.
 
 No Azure Storage account, MongoDB service, Container Apps, API Management,
 virtual network, private endpoint, or Application Insights resource is needed
 to run this local demo. Do not create new Azure resources, change SKUs, or
 deploy new models without authorization. The project’s authorization boundary
 is documented in [ADR-0007](docs/architecture/decisions/adr-0007-demo-delivery-mode.md).
 
 Official setup references:
 
 * [Create an Azure AI Search service](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/search-create-service-portal)
 * [Vector search in Azure AI Search](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/vector-search-overview)
 * [Create a Microsoft Foundry project and deploy a model](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/tutorials/quickstart-create-foundry-resources)
 
 ### Start the stack
 
 From the repository root, copy the example configuration only if you do not
 already have a local `.env` file. Fill the Foundry and Search values in `.env`;
 do not commit it or print its contents:
 
 ```powershell
 if (-not (Test-Path .env)) { Copy-Item .env.example .env }
 ```
 
 Keep `CHAT_TEMPERATURE` empty and
 `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_QUERY_RESPONSE_RETENTION_ENABLED=false`. The chat client omits
 temperature for `gpt-5` and reasoning deployments.
 
 Start the Podman machine if it is stopped, then build and start the services:
 
 ```powershell
 podman machine list
 # Run only when the machine is stopped:
 podman machine start
 podman compose up --build -d
 ```
 
 Open [http://127.0.0.1:3000](http://127.0.0.1:3000). Check the API at
 [http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz](http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz) and coverage at
 [http://127.0.0.1:8000/catalog/coverage](http://127.0.0.1:8000/catalog/coverage).
 The browser never calls FastAPI directly.
 
 If the local MongoDB volume is empty, run the bounded ingestion pass and then
 index the canonical pages into Azure AI Search:
 
 ```powershell
 podman compose run --rm api uv run --no-sync python scripts/run_source_ingestion.py
 podman compose run --rm api uv run --no-sync python scripts/index_documents.py
 ```
 
 These commands use only the approved source map, robots policy, freshness
 checks, request budget, and backoff. The index script creates or updates the
 versioned demo index. Ingestion uses real public sources and configured Foundry
 deployments, so follow the budgets and limits in the
 [local runbook](docs/operations/local-development.md).
 
 Stop the project while preserving its MongoDB and Azurite volumes:
 
 ```powershell
 podman compose stop --timeout 30
 ```
 
 Do not use `podman compose down --volumes` unless you intend to delete local
 data. See the runbook for restart and cleanup details.
 
 ## Configuration and environment variables
 
 `.env.example` is the canonical template. The table covers the application
 variables in that file and the additional web runtime variable. Values shown
 in the template are examples; edit a local `.env` and never commit credentials.
 Compose passes `.env` only to the API container and overrides the MongoDB and
 manifest/source-map paths for the container network.
 
 ### Application and privacy
 
 | Variable | Purpose and local-demo guidance |
 |---|---|
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_ENVIRONMENT` | Application environment label. Use `local` for the Compose demo. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_QUERY_RESPONSE_RETENTION_ENABLED` | Enables query/response storage. Keep `false`; retention is not part of the demo. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_QUERY_RESPONSE_RETENTION_DAYS` | Proposed retention TTL if retention is approved and enabled. It has no effect while retention is off. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_QUERY_REVIEWER_ROLE` | Reviewer role required by configuration if retention is enabled. Leave empty for the demo. |
 
 ### Catalog and queue workflow
 
 These settings configure the catalog-discovery and queue workflow. They are
 not needed for normal chat startup or the source-map-based documentation
 ingestion job.
 
 | Variable | Purpose and local-demo guidance |
 |---|---|
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_CATALOG_LISTING_URL` | Product listing endpoint used by catalog discovery. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_CATALOG_SEARCH_URL` | Catalog search endpoint. Do not add authentication or bypass access controls. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_CATALOG_FEED_URL` | Catalog feed endpoint used by the catalog fallback. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_CATALOG_MAX_PAGES` | Maximum catalog pages to process. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_CATALOG_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Timeout for catalog HTTP requests. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_CATALOG_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` | Maximum catalog response body size. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_MAX_DEMO_PRODUCTS` | Maximum manifest size; hard-limited to 100. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_MANIFEST_SEED` | Stable seed used when selecting a reproducible manifest sample. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_AZURITE_QUEUE_CONNECTION_STRING` | Local Azurite Queue Storage connection string for queue-based catalog processing. Not required for chat. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_INGESTION_QUEUE_NAME` | Queue name used by the catalog ingestion workflow. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_POISON_DEQUEUE_COUNT` | Maximum dequeue attempts before a message is treated as poison. |
 
 ### Source ingestion and local storage
 
 | Variable | Purpose and local-demo guidance |
 |---|---|
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_MANIFEST_PATH` | Approved product manifest JSON path. Compose overrides it with the path copied into the API image. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SOURCE_MAP_PATH` | Approved documentation source map JSON path. Compose overrides it with the path copied into the API image. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_MONGODB_URI` | MongoDB connection string. Use `mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017` from the host; Compose overrides it inside the API container to `mongodb://mongodb:27017`. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SOURCE_USER_AGENT` | User-Agent sent by the bounded source ingestion worker. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SOURCE_REQUEST_BUDGET` | Maximum HTTP requests per ingestion run; default 400, hard maximum 2,000. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SOURCE_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | Minimum delay between requests to a host. The configured minimum is one second. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SOURCE_MAX_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS` | Maximum delay honored from a source `Retry-After` header. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SOURCE_SUCCESS_FRESHNESS_HOURS` | Period during which a successfully fetched page is reused without another request. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SOURCE_TRANSIENT_FAILURE_BACKOFF_HOURS` | Backoff after a transient source failure. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SOURCE_PERMANENT_FAILURE_BACKOFF_DAYS` | Backoff after a permanent or protected-source failure. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SOURCE_FAIL_FAST_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES` | Consecutive page failures before the worker stops processing that product. |
 
 ### Foundry models and chat
 
 | Variable | Purpose and local-demo guidance |
 |---|---|
 | `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | Foundry OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, ending in `/openai/v1`. |
 | `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` | Key used by the server for Foundry chat and embeddings. Keep it in `.env` only. |
 | `AZURE_OPENAI_CHAT_DEPLOYMENT` | Exact Foundry chat deployment name. The template uses `gpt-5`. |
 | `AZURE_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_DEPLOYMENT` | Exact Foundry embedding deployment name. The template uses `text-embedding-3-small`. |
 | `AZURE_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_ENDPOINT` | OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint. Use the endpoint for the configured Foundry resource. |
 | `CHAT_TEMPERATURE` | Leave empty. `gpt-5` rejects temperature, and the client omits it for `gpt-5` and other reasoning deployments. |
 
 ### Azure AI Search
 
 | Variable | Purpose and local-demo guidance |
 |---|---|
 | `AZURE_AI_SEARCH_ENDPOINT` | Azure AI Search service endpoint, such as `https://<service>.search.windows.net`. |
 | `AZURE_AI_SEARCH_API_KEY` | Server-side Search key used by the application for indexing and retrieval. Keep it out of browser code and source control. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_EMBEDDING_MODEL_VERSION` | Embedding model identifier included in the versioned Search index configuration. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` | Vector size expected by the Search schema; use `1536` for `text-embedding-3-small` in this demo. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_DEMO_INDEX_BASE` | Base name for the versioned demo index. Keep it under the `product-support-*` namespace. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_TEST_INDEX_BASE` | Base name for disposable live-test indexes. Keep it under the `product-support-test-*` namespace. |
 
 ### Additional runtime and script settings
 
 | Variable | Purpose and local-demo guidance |
 |---|---|
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_API_BASE_URL` | Server-side URL used by Next.js to call FastAPI. Compose sets `http://api:8000`; when running Next.js on the host, use `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Never expose it as a `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variable. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_ENDPOINT` | Optional Search endpoint alias. `scripts/apply_search_index.py` requires this variable. It can also override `AZURE_AI_SEARCH_ENDPOINT` in application settings. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_ADMIN_KEY` | Optional Search admin-key alias. `scripts/apply_search_index.py` requires this variable; it can also override `AZURE_AI_SEARCH_API_KEY`. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_EMBEDDING_BASE_URL` | Optional alias that overrides `AZURE_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_ENDPOINT` in application settings. |
 | `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` | Optional alias that overrides `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` for embedding requests. |
 
 ## Repository structure
 
 ```text
 product-support-agent/
 ├── .github/
 │   ├── agents/                 # Repository-specific Copilot agents
 │   ├── instructions/           # Python, Bicep, and CI security guidance
 │   ├── prompts/                # Review and threat-model prompts
 │   └── workflows/              # GitHub Actions validation workflow
 ├── apps/
 │   └── web/                    # Next.js and TypeScript frontend
 │       └── src/
 │           ├── app/            # Pages, server route handlers, and styles
 │           ├── components/     # Chat and UI components
 │           └── lib/            # Server-side API clients and helpers
 ├── docs/
 │   ├── architecture/           # Architecture, decisions, risks, and requirements
 │   │   └── decisions/          # ADRs
 │   ├── chat-sessions/          # Sample conversation records
 │   ├── operations/             # Runbooks, manifests, source map, and evaluation
 │   └── security/               # Threat model, privacy, and security posture
 ├── scripts/                    # Ingestion, indexing, evaluation, and maintenance
 ├── src/
 │   └── product_support_agent/  # Python domain logic and FastAPI backend
 │       └── api/                # HTTP application and endpoint wiring
 ├── tests/
 │   ├── evaluation/             # Versioned evaluation questions
 │   ├── integration/            # Opt-in live Search integration tests
 │   └── unit/                   # Offline deterministic tests
 ├── .env.example                # Documented local environment template
 ├── Containerfile               # API container image
 ├── apps/web/Containerfile      # Web container image
 ├── compose.yaml                # Loopback-bound local demo stack
 ├── pyproject.toml              # Python dependencies and tool configuration
 └── uv.lock                     # Locked Python dependency graph
 ```
 
 There is currently no `infra/` directory or deployed Azure application stack.
 The Azure architecture and future infrastructure work are documented in the
 [implementation plan](docs/implementation-plan.md) and
 [architecture overview](docs/architecture/architecture-overview.md).
 
 ## Architecture and data flow
 
 1. The source worker reads only
    [`phase-3-source-map-v1.json`](docs/operations/phase-3-source-map-v1.json)
    and stores permitted canonical pages and fetch state in local MongoDB.
 2. `scripts/index_documents.py` creates or updates a versioned Azure AI Search
    index and writes chunks/vectors using the Foundry embedding deployment.
 3. The browser sends chat requests to Next.js. The server-side route calls
    FastAPI; the agent retrieves filtered evidence from Azure AI Search and
    calls the Foundry chat deployment.
 4. The API binds cited evidence IDs to retrieved source URLs. The UI renders
    answers as plain text and links from the citation list only.
 
 See the [architecture overview](docs/architecture/architecture-overview.md)
 for diagrams and [ADR-0005](docs/architecture/decisions/adr-0005-ui-and-backend-technology.md)
 for the UI/backend boundary.
 
 ## Quality assurance
 
 Install the Python development dependencies from the repository root:
 
 ```powershell
 uv sync --all-groups
 ```
 
 Routine Python validation is offline by default:
 
 ```powershell
 uv run ruff format --check .
 uv run ruff check .
 uv run mypy src/product_support_agent scripts
 uv run pytest
 uv run bandit -q -r src scripts
 ```
 
 For web changes, run from `apps/web`:
 
 ```powershell
 npm ci
 npm run lint
 npm run typecheck
 npm run build
 ```
 
 The default pytest configuration excludes live tests. The marked Search
 integration test creates a dedicated `product-support-test-*` index and removes
 it after the test:
 
 ```powershell
 uv run pytest -m live
 ```
 
 Run the local evaluation after Compose is healthy:
 
 ```powershell
 uv run python scripts/run_evaluation.py --api-url http://127.0.0.1:8000
 ```
 
 See the [evaluation report](docs/operations/phase-6-evaluation-v1.md) for the
 current baseline and [implementation plan](docs/implementation-plan.md) for
 phase completion evidence.

 ### Application and privacy
 
 | Variable | Purpose and local-demo guidance |

 ### Catalog and queue workflow
 
 These settings configure the catalog-discovery and queue workflow. They are

 | Variable | Purpose and local-demo guidance |

 ## Architecture and data flow
 
 1. The source worker reads only
    [`phase-3-source-map-v1.json`](docs/operations/phase-3-source-map-v1.json)
    and stores permitted canonical pages and fetch state in local MongoDB.
 2. `scripts/index_documents.py` creates or updates a versioned Azure AI Search
    index and writes chunks/vectors using the Foundry embedding deployment.
 3. The browser sends chat requests to Next.js. The server-side route calls
    FastAPI; the agent retrieves filtered evidence from Azure AI Search and
    calls the Foundry chat deployment.
 4. The API binds cited evidence IDs to retrieved source URLs. The UI renders
    answers as plain text and links from the citation list only.
 
 See the [architecture overview](docs/architecture/architecture-overview.md)
 for diagrams and [ADR-0005](docs/architecture/decisions/adr-0005-ui-and-backend-technology.md)

 ---
 title: Local Development Runbook
 description: Run the product support demo locally with Podman Compose
 author: Product Support Agent Team
 ms.date: 2026-11-22

   - local development

 This runbook starts the local demo against the existing Microsoft Foundry and
 Azure AI Search services. The browser talks only to Next.js; Next.js calls
 FastAPI over the Compose network. No query or response history is stored.
 
 ## Prerequisites and environment
 
 * Podman with a running machine and a working `podman compose` provider.
 * Network access to the user's Foundry and Azure AI Search endpoints.
 * Valid deployment and Search credentials in a local `.env` file.
 * `uv` 0.13.9 or later for running the evaluation and Python checks.
 
 ### Azure resources to prepare
 
 The local demo requires access to two Azure services:
 
 * Microsoft Foundry with a chat deployment (`gpt-5`) and an embedding
   deployment (`text-embedding-3-small`). Record the OpenAI-compatible endpoint,
   API key, and exact deployment names.
 * Azure AI Search with a service endpoint and admin key for server-side index
   creation, indexing, and retrieval. The indexing script creates the versioned
   `product-support-demo-*` index; live tests use a separate
   `product-support-test-*` index.
 
 Vector search is supported across current Search tiers, but quotas, capacity,
 pricing, and other features differ. Check the current service limits and costs.
 This project did not verify semantic ranking availability. MongoDB and Azurite
 run locally in Compose; no Azure Storage account, database, network, or
 application-hosting resources are required. See the
 [README Azure setup overview](../../README.md#azure-resources-for-a-local-only-demo)
 and the linked Microsoft setup guides there.
 
 Creating Azure resources, changing service tiers, or deploying new models may
 incur spend and requires the authorization described in
 [ADR-0007](../architecture/decisions/adr-0007-demo-delivery-mode.md).
 
 From a clean checkout, copy `.env.example` once, then fill in the existing
 deployment and Search values locally. Do not overwrite an existing `.env`:
 
 ```powershell
 if (-not (Test-Path .env)) { Copy-Item .env.example .env }
 ```
 
 Required settings in `.env` are:
 
 * `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` (OpenAI-compatible endpoint ending in `/openai/v1`),
   `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, and `AZURE_OPENAI_CHAT_DEPLOYMENT`.
 * `AZURE_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_ENDPOINT` and
   `AZURE_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_DEPLOYMENT`.
 * `AZURE_AI_SEARCH_ENDPOINT` and `AZURE_AI_SEARCH_API_KEY`.
 * `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_EMBEDDING_MODEL_VERSION`,
   `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` (`1536`), and
   `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_SEARCH_DEMO_INDEX_BASE` (`product-support-demo`).
 * `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_MONGODB_URI` may remain
   `mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017` in the host `.env`; Compose overrides it inside
   the API container with `mongodb://mongodb:27017`.
 
 Leave `CHAT_TEMPERATURE` empty. The gpt-5 chat deployment rejects a temperature
 parameter, so the chat client omits it. Query/response retention must remain
 disabled.
 
 Compose passes `.env` only to the API service using `env_file`; secrets are not
 baked into either image. The web service receives only
 `PRODUCT_SUPPORT_API_BASE_URL=http://api:8000`. The API image contains the
 approved manifest and source map JSON files, not the rest of `docs/`.
 
 ## Start the demo
 
 Start the Podman machine only if it is stopped:
 
 ```powershell
 podman machine list
 # If it is not running:
 podman machine start
 ```
 
 From the repository root, one command builds and starts MongoDB, Azurite, the
 API, and the web app. Health checks gate startup order, and published ports bind
 only to loopback:
 
 ```powershell
 podman compose up --build -d
 ```
 
 Open `http://127.0.0.1:3000`. The coverage page reports the 100-product
 manifest, the 10 products with approved public sources, and the current
 indexed-page count. The API health endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz`;
 coverage metadata is at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/catalog/coverage`. The browser
 does not call FastAPI directly.
 
 An existing local database volume may already contain the 300 canonical
 pages ingested for the 10 covered products. A new empty MongoDB volume needs a
 bounded ingestion and indexing pass before chat can answer:
 
 ```powershell
 podman compose run --rm api uv run --no-sync python scripts/run_source_ingestion.py
 podman compose run --rm api uv run --no-sync python scripts/index_documents.py
 ```
 
 Ingestion uses only
 [`phase-3-source-map-v1.json`](./phase-3-source-map-v1.json), the configured
 request budget, robots policy, freshness checks, and backoff. Indexing creates
 or updates the `product-support-demo-*` Search index from canonical MongoDB
 documents using the Foundry embedding deployment. These commands do not
 provision Azure resources. Rerun indexing after ingesting new or changed pages.
 
 Ask a question in the web page and optionally filter to an indexed product.
